plan.title: rfc(session,swarm): spawned work takes its own worktree; master occupancy is the exception and must be released

narratives.Description: The recut still cannot bind as written. Split the spawn occupancy seam, drop the ors, make terminal release dispatcher-owned with an incarnation, and add execution-root re-root as a seventh leg.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Spawned work and mutating parent sessions must take their own git worktree. The primary checkout (`master`) occupancy lease is the exception, used only when that tree is actually required, and must be released when the session is done. Today multiple multi-agent tabs sit on the same tree, contend for one `.deft/occupancy.json`, and then try to grant a child from another host onto that lease. That path fails closed as designed, and agents fall into a session-id rewrite fight instead of isolating the worker.

## Context

Directive occupancy is per worktree path (`#3433`). Canonical owners are `host:<provider>:v1:<base64url(raw-id)>` (`#3611`). `occupancy:grant` refuses a child whose payload is the owner's own host session under a second provider (`#3954`):

> occupancy:grant refuses the child id …: it carries this lease owner's own host session (…) under provider …. That is a self-grant across a provider prefix, and the child it names cannot exist.

On a `host-env` host (Grok), parent and dispatched children are different actors and each is supposed to claim **its own worktree** (`commands.md` occupancy, `#3954` / `#3999`). Membership onto the parent's lease is not the default there.

That contract is not what interactive tabs do. Several Claude / Cursor / Grok conversations stay in the primary checkout, `session:start` claims master, and a later Grok (or other) spawn tries to join that lease. Multiple tabs make the contention visible: writes deny, steal becomes the entry ritual, and occupancy is not released when a tab finishes.

## Measured (just now)

A Grok session working in this repo hit:

1. **Self-grant across provider prefix refused.** The same UUID cannot be granted as a `grok` child of a `claude` owner. That refusal is correct (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts` around the `#3954` item-3 check).
2. **Ownership flip-flop.** Presentation (`DEFT_SESSION_ID` / `--session-id` / what the process claims) and the lease (who `.deft/occupancy.json` names) are decoupled. Lifecycle hooks rewrite `--session-id` one way; the write-gate sibling may present another (`#3873` residue: hook process env vs agent shell).
3. Agents then try to "fix" the dual-probe (export, steal, re-grant, re-prefix) instead of leaving the occupied tree.

The clean path is to stop joining the foreign-host master lease and make the worker self-contained: own worktree, own occupancy claim, release on terminal.

## Expected behavior

- A mutating session, and every spawned implementation / review / fix worker, **selects or creates a worktree** before claiming occupancy.
- The primary checkout is used only when that tree is the work (release cut, branch-policy restore, operator-directed default-branch work, orientation that is `--read-only`).
- On DONE / terminal / `session:end`, the session **releases** the occupancy it claimed (`occupancy:release` / `session:end`; child trees via the `#3999` compare-and-release path).
- Cross-host spawn does **not** attempt `occupancy:grant` of a Grok id onto a Claude (or other provider) owner of master. It creates a worktree and claims that tree.
- Several concurrent multi-agent tabs do not serialize on one master lease.

## Actual behavior

- Interactive parents default to the primary checkout and claim its exclusive lease.
- Spawned agents inherit that cwd / try to grant onto that lease.
- `#3954` correctly refuses the cross-prefix self-grant.
- The recovery agents follow is the dual-probe / steal / re-prefix dance, which keeps tripping occupancy rather than isolating work.
- Finished tabs often leave the lease in place, so the next tab steals or waits. `#3604` named ghost leases; `#3999` closed child-on-terminal for recorded swarm dispatches, not ad-hoc parent tabs.

## Why existing issues do not cover this

| Issue | What it owns | Why this is separate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#3032` | Through-merge parent must not implement as the leaf | Does not bind worktree-default for ordinary tabs, issue filing, or cross-host spawn |
| `#3954` | One actor-resolution chain; refuse impossible grants | The refusal is correct. This issue is the dispatch posture that avoids needing the grant |
| `#3999` | Release a recorded child's lease on `phase: terminal` | Swarm/recorded dispatch only; does not force worktree selection or parent-tab release |
| `#4020` | Forge-only sessions should not claim | Complementary (don't claim master if you will not write it). Does not say mutating spawn takes a worktree |
| `#3873` | Hook sibling env vs host-published owner | Fighting that dual-probe is the anti-pattern this issue refuses |
| `#3613` | Occupancy model-gap tracker | This is caller/dispatch posture, not a missing lease dimension |

## Proposed fix (posture, then mechanism)

1. **Dispatch rule.** Spawn isolation is a worktree (host `isolation=worktree` / `git worktree add` / swarm worktree-map) **before** occupancy claim. Fail closed if the child would share the primary checkout with a live foreign occupant.
2. **Master is the exception.** Document the allow-list (release pipeline, policy restore, explicit operator default-branch work, `--read-only` orientation). ⊗ Default mutation or spawn onto the occupied primary tree.
3. **Release on done.** Parent tabs and ad-hoc workers run `occupancy:release` / `session:end` when they stop mutating. Reuse `#3999` compare-and-release for recorded children; add the missing parent-tab / non-swarm spawn close-out.
4. **Do not grant across hosts on master.** Printed recovery for the `#3954` self-grant refusal should name "create/claim a worktree" first, not steal or re-prefix.

## Non-goals

- Weakening the `#3954` self-grant refusal
- Making occupancy authenticate hosts (it stays a cooperative bearer-id, `#3755`)
- Auto-waiting on a peer parent (`#4016` closed: claim is already atomic)
- Cleaning the existing worktree pile (`#3860`)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Swarm skill + preamble state: spawned mutating workers take a worktree; sharing the primary checkout with a live occupant is refuse, not grant-across-host.
- [ ] `occupancy:grant` self-grant-across-prefix remediation names worktree isolation first.
- [ ] Ad-hoc / host spawn (Grok `spawn_subagent`, Cursor Task, Claude subagent) has a documented close-out that releases the worker tree occupancy on terminal, not only `task swarm:launch` cohorts.
- [ ] Parent tab on the primary checkout that is done mutating releases occupancy; a second tab can claim without steal when the first has ended.
- [ ] Master remains usable for the documented exception list without requiring a worktree.
- [ ] A regression covers: Claude-owned primary lease + Grok child id with the same raw UUID is refused, and the printed recovery does not tell the Grok session to steal master.

## Origin

Operator request 2026-09-01 after live contention with several multi-agent tabs on the directive primary checkout, including a Grok session refused as a grok child of a claude owner.

## Verdict

The posture is directionally right and mostly already written for `host-env` actors. It does **not** bind as drafted. Binding fails on missing enforcement and on parent-tab close-out that has no terminal observer. Fix those two, then the remediation / primary-tree / payload-host sharpenings can land with it.

Open critique of the issue premise (spawned mutating work takes its own worktree; primary occupancy is the exception and must be released). Not bound to the triage refutation-target field.

## Inventory (existing mechanisms)

- `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts` at `f96963e9`: per-worktree lease (#3433); cooperative bearer-id (#3755); `host-env` parents/children are different actors and "claims its own worktree, which is where the dispatch envelope already puts it"; `OccupancyGrant` docs say children land in their own worktree "**not because anything enforces it**"; `#3954` item-3 refuses same-raw-id re-prefix across provider (`self-grant across a provider prefix… child it names cannot exist`) with **no** worktree recovery line; stranger remediation (`formatOccupancyRemediation`) already offers "use another worktree" alongside grant and steal.
- `content/commands.md` occupancy bullets: same host-env own-worktree rule; `#3999` compare-and-release only for recorded children under `.deft/child-occupancy/` on `phase: terminal`; **Lifetime and enforcement boundaries** explicitly: "spawn tools remain outside occupancy enforcement."
- `packages/core/src/session/child-occupancy.ts`: `releaseChildOccupancyOnTerminal` is compare-and-release for recorded host-env children; `payload-skip` on shared-id hosts; missing record → no release.
- Swarm Phase 0 (`content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-0.md`): through-merge / `#3032` requires launch path with "worktree isolation when available" for story drive-to:merge-ready — not ordinary interactive tabs, issue filing, or cross-host ad-hoc spawn.
- Related issues as cited: `#3032` closed (through-merge parent⊗leaf); `#3954` closed (actor chain + impossible-grant refuse); `#3999` closed (recorded-child terminal release); `#4020` open (forge-only should not claim). Issue table correctly separates them.

## Injection / swarm lens

Target changes authority (who may mutate the primary tree), identity (`host:<provider>:v1:…` / cross-host grant), concurrency (multi-tab), worktrees, and shared state (`.deft/occupancy.json`). Lens fires.

Under cooperative bearer-id, remediation that still leads with steal / re-prefix is an escalation path: a confused or injected agent takes the primary lease instead of isolating. Worktree-first recovery is load-bearing safety text, not copy polish. Same-tree cross-host membership would also share dirty HEAD and ritual state across providers — another reason isolation beats grant-onto-master.

## 1. blocks-the-design — no enforcement surface for "worktree before claim"

**Evidence:** occupancy.ts states worktree placement is envelope convention, not enforcement; commands.md states spawn tools remain outside occupancy enforcement. PreToolUse already matches spawn tools for the pre-`start_agent` gate stack, but that stack does not require a non-primary worktree before claim. Skill/preamble MUST is the same class `#3032` already used for through-merge — and this issue's measured failure is interactive/ad-hoc paths that ignore that prose and fight dual-probe instead.

**Failure mode:** Claude-owned primary + Grok (or second tab) still lands on the same cwd, hits `#3954` / deny / steal, and the dual-probe dance recurs after the docs land. "Fail closed if the child would share the primary checkout with a live foreign occupant" has nowhere to run today.

**Disposition:** lean cannot bind until it names a deterministic control — e.g. extend the spawn PreToolUse path to require a resolved worktree path ≠ primary before mutation claim, and/or refuse claim when cwd is the main worktree and a live foreign occupant exists for spawn-class callers — **or** explicitly demote the fail-closed AC to advisory and drop the refuse-not-grant language. Do not close this with "agents will follow the skill."

## 2. blocks-the-design — parent-tab / ad-hoc release AC has no terminal observer

**Evidence:** Ordinary end is `occupancy:release` / `session:end` (#3604), both caller-driven. `#3999` release fires only when orchestration observes `phase: terminal` **and** a child-occupancy record exists for that agent/worktree. Interactive parent tabs that stop chatting do not emit that transition; ad-hoc `spawn_subagent` / Cursor Task / Claude subagent paths that skip `recordChildOccupancyLease` get `missing-record` and leave the lease until TTL/steal. That is exactly the stranding class `#3999`'s issue body measured.

**Failure mode:** AC "Parent tab on the primary checkout that is done mutating releases occupancy; a second tab can claim without steal" fails in the common case (tab closed / conversation ended with no `session:end`). Steal remains the entry ritual; ghost leases persist inside the 20-minute TTL / 12-hour age cap.

**Disposition:** either (a) deposit a host SessionEnd (or equivalent) that runs release for the presented owner, plus require ad-hoc spawn to record child-occupancy the way swarm dispatch does, or (b) rewrite the AC to "when `session:end` / recorded terminal fires" and keep TTL/steal as the reclaim for abandoned tabs. Binding the stronger AC without a terminal path is false green.

## 3. sharpens-framing — "master" vs primary checkout path

**Evidence:** Issue summary/expected behavior mix "primary checkout (`master`)" with an allow-list of default-branch / release / policy-restore work. Occupancy keys on `worktree_path`, not branch tip. A primary clone sitting on a feature branch is still the contended exclusive lease.

**Failure mode:** Agents treat "not on master" as license to mutate the main worktree path, or refuse legitimate default-branch work that is not on the primary path.

**Disposition:** redefine the exception as the **main worktree path** (non-linked checkout / git-common-dir parent), with branch-shaped allow-list items as reasons that path may be claimed — not as the definition of the exception.

## 4. sharpens-framing — payload-host same-id spawn underspecified

**Evidence:** commands.md / occupancy.ts: on `payload` hosts (Claude, Cursor, Codex) parent and subagents share one id — nothing to grant; parent's release would drop a same-id child mid-flight. Issue fail-closed and recovery text center on foreign occupant + cross-prefix grant refusal (the Grok-on-Claude incident).

**Failure mode:** Same-provider spawn keeps inheriting primary cwd; contention becomes shared-owner mutation on one tree rather than a refused grant, so the printed `#3954` recovery never fires and the new remediation never teaches the fix.

**Disposition:** state worktree-before-claim for spawned mutating workers on **all** identity-source kinds. Keep the cross-prefix remediation change as the host-env incident fix, not as the whole rule.

## 5. sharpens-framing — compose with `#4020` or absorb its carve-out

**Evidence:** `#4020` (open) is forge-only / non-writing sessions still claiming the exclusive lease. Multi-tab contention that motivated `#4066` includes design-critique, triage, and issue-shaping tabs that never need the tree.

**Failure mode:** Shipping `#4066` worktree-for-spawn alone still serializes non-mutating tabs on the primary lease; steal remains the handshake between a critique tab and a later implementer.

**Disposition:** sequence `#4020` as a sibling in the lean, or fold "non-mutating / forge-only sessions do not claim" into the exception list as already-owned by `#4020` so this issue does not re-litigate it.

## 6. footnote — self-grant refusal text gap is already in AC

`grantOccupancyMembership` at the `#3954` same-raw-id check ends at "cannot exist" with no worktree line. Stranger remediation already mentions another worktree. AC item 2 already demands worktree-first recovery on that refuse path — track as implementation detail once findings 1–2 bind.

## Road not taken

**Chosen:** worktree isolation before occupancy claim; primary path exceptional; no cross-host grant onto primary.

**Rejected (strongest):** membership-first same-tree — parent on primary grants a *distinct* foreign-host child id onto that lease so both share one checkout.

**Steelman:** one working tree, no further `#3860` worktree pile, parent keeps owner-only admin, matches deliberate same-tree membership the grant API already allows.

**What would flip:** hosts mint truly distinct child raw ids (no re-prefix of the owner's UUID), parents grant before spawn as ritual, grant budget (32 × 4h vs 20-minute lease) does not exhaust under busy dispatch, and shared dirty HEAD / ritual across hosts is acceptable.

**Why reject now:** measured incident is re-prefix of the same raw UUID (exactly what `#3954` refuses); grant-on-every-dispatch math is already documented as unaffordable; `#3032` / swarm Phase 0 already want worktree isolation for implement leaves; cross-host same-tree shares mutation authority under cooperative bearer-id.

## Bind judgment

Posture can bind only after findings 1 and 2 are resolved in the lean (named enforcement surface + honest close-out AC). Findings 3–5 must reshape wording/scope. Finding 6 is covered by existing AC once the blockers land. Do not weaken the `#3954` refusal.

Verdict: the posture does not bind as written. At f96963e9ce2a9bab41fdc2646e67380e8bf0dbaa, the refusal is sound, but the proposed rule lacks the pre-claim and terminal authorities needed to make isolation reliable across ordinary host spawns.

blocks-the-design - Evidence: packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts describes host-env parent and child as separate actors that claim their own worktrees, while content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-0.md says task swarm:launch claims "this worktree" before it emits the manifest; the worktree map is only an optional later input. The acceptance criteria ask for skill/preamble posture, but name no deterministic pre-claim selector or gate for an ad-hoc host spawn. Failure mode: a mutation parent launched from the primary checkout can claim that checkout before any worker worktree is selected, and an opaque host spawn can inherit that cwd. The proposed master exception then relies on an actor recognizing an exception after it already holds the lease. Disposition: do not bind until the design names one pre-claim control that resolves or creates the target worktree first, rejects mutation or swarm on the primary root unless an explicit exception is presented, and makes unknown host spawn shapes refuse rather than silently inherit cwd. Its regression must exercise the launch order, not only the existing cross-prefix grant refusal.

blocks-the-design - Evidence: #3999 records that a compliant dispatched worker exited with a live lease and explicitly rejects a documentation-only worker duty; occupancy.ts says recorded-child close-out is dispatcher lifecycle, and owner-only release is intentionally not transferable. This issue nevertheless makes terminal release a general worker/parent-tab expectation without defining a durable dispatcher record and verified terminal callback for ad-hoc host spawns. Failure mode: an ad-hoc worker's terminal event is unobserved, or it is told to release but never executes the command, leaving the claimed worktree unavailable until expiry: the measured #3999 class under a new name. Disposition: bind release only to a recorded dispatch/lease tuple and a dispatcher or platform terminal callback that compare-and-releases that exact worktree; an unsupported host must fail closed for mutating dispatch, or remain explicitly out of the guarantee. Test claim -> terminal -> no lease for both swarm and one ad-hoc adapter.

sharpens-framing - Injection/swarm lens: the selector and callback are authority boundaries, not convenience plumbing. A child-supplied cwd, worktree-map entry, session id, or terminal signal must not be able to select the primary checkout or release a different live lease. Derive the allowed worktree from a parent-owned dispatch record, validate it is the allocated path, and compare owner/id/path at release. Otherwise an injected envelope can turn the anti-contention posture into a cross-worktree release primitive. Disposition: specify these bindings in the mechanism and tests; do not rely on reviewer attention.

Road not taken: a universal preamble instruction to create a worktree and release before exit. Its strongest case is broad host coverage with little engine work. I reject it because both operations are authority-bearing and #3999 already demonstrates that a correct worker can finish without a lifecycle release. I would flip if every supported host supplied an authenticated, tested terminal callback that executes the same recorded compare-and-release path and the pre-claim selector was mandatory at spawn.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-01T22:00:39Z)

model: claude-opus-5

Open critique, round 1, fresh. Read at `f96963e9`. Anchors re-run rather than cited: I executed `applyWorktreeOccupancy`, `grantOccupancyMembership`, `evaluateOccupancyWriteGate` and `releaseOccupancy` against throwaway git trees under a Node type-stripping harness (no repo writes), and read `dispatcher.ts` / `child-occupancy.ts` at that SHA.

**Verdict: the posture is right in direction and cannot bind as written.** Worktree-by-default, master-as-exception, release-on-done is the correct shape. But the measured incident's cause is not tree sharing, and three of the six acceptance criteria are either unreachable or green-without-behaviour on the host arm they matter most on.

### F1 — Worktree isolation does not remove the ownership flip-flop; `DEFT_SESSION_ID` inheritance does

`blocks-the-design`

**Evidence (measured).** A child in a brand-new, exclusively-owned worktree, with `DEFT_SESSION_ID` inherited across the spawn boundary and its own host publishing `GROK_SESSION_ID`:

```
resolve: {"sessionId":"11111111-...-555555555555","source":"environment",
          "disagreeingHostOwner":"host:grok:v1:MTExMTExMTEt..."}
claim: claimed   lease owner: 11111111-...-555555555555
gate allow: false
  Worktree occupied by session 11111111-...-555555555555 ...
  This process presented session host:grok:v1:MTExMTExMTEt..., which neither holds that
  lease nor has a write grant on it.
  Stay read-only ..., use another worktree, ask the occupant for a write grant ..., or run a
  confirmed owner transition (`session:start --steal --confirm --occupant 11111111-... ...`).
release: denied code: 1   (same text)
```

No shared primary checkout. No cross-host grant. No contention. The child is a stranger on the tree it just created, and the printed recovery tells it to steal from itself or beg a grant from an occupant that is itself. Mechanism: `resolvePresentedIdentity` puts `DEFT_SESSION_ID` **above** the host-published owner unconditionally (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:540-562`), the claim path goes through it (`resolveOccupancySessionId`, `occupancy.ts:593-597`), and the write gate takes its actor from the host payload while deliberately dropping the ambient env when the host is authoritative (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:1245-1257`, `env: actor?.hostAuthoritative === true ? {} : environ`). Two surfaces, two answers, one session.

**Failure mode.** Every mandated leg of the fix runs and the incident recurs one tree over: worker takes its own worktree (rule 1), claims it (rule 1), is refused its first gated write, is refused `occupancy:release` on terminal (rule 3 / AC4), and is handed the steal text as the only runnable move (rule 4's exact anti-pattern). The tree is then held to the 20-minute heartbeat expiry by a session that cannot release it.

**Disposition consequence.** Rule 1 and AC4 cannot both hold without a spawn-boundary identity rule. The issue parks that under `#3873` as "the dual-probe this issue refuses to fight" — but the dual probe reproduces *inside* the isolated tree, so parking it does not remove it. Either add a rule (unset or re-publish `DEFT_SESSION_ID` at the spawn boundary, or make the host-published owner authoritative at claim on host-authoritative hosts, mirroring what `dispatcher.ts:1256-1257` already does on the write path), or strike AC4 as out of reach.

### F2 — The lifecycle execution-root gate denies exactly the move rule 1 mandates, and points the child back at master

`blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** `lifecycleExecutionRootCheck` (`dispatcher.ts:1860-1911`) realpath-binds every execution-directory field against `input.projectRoot` — the *hook payload* root. On mismatch the dispatcher denies the lifecycle command outright (`dispatcher.ts:2005-2021`), with: `Run the lifecycle command from <payload root> so policy, lease, and ritual state target the same worktree.` `content/commands.md:423` records the same rule ("an execution-root mismatch on an owner-requiring command always denies").

**Failure mode.** A host spawn that inherits the parent's payload root, `cd`s into `.deft-scratch/worktrees/<x>` and runs `deft session:start` there is denied before it can claim, and the denial text instructs it back to the primary checkout. That is the `host-env` arm the origin incident came from. Claude Code's `isolation: worktree` re-roots the payload, so it is unaffected — which is precisely why a host-agnostic MUST is the wrong shape here.

**Disposition consequence.** AC1 is stated host-agnostically and cannot bind that way. It needs a per-host precondition: the dispatch surface must re-root the hook payload onto the child worktree, and hosts that cannot are outside rule 1 (or must dispatch through `swarm:launch`'s worktree map, which does re-root). What would flip this: evidence that every dispatch surface in play re-roots the payload. I looked and found only the Claude-side knob.

### F3 — AC3 and AC4 are satisfiable with prose and zero behaviour on the payload arm

`blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** `releaseChildOccupancyOnTerminal` returns `payload-skip` **unconditionally** on `identitySourceKind === "payload"` (`packages/core/src/session/child-occupancy.ts:230-232`), before it ever looks at the recorded tree. The kind is stamped at claim as `grokRaw.length > 0 ? "host-env" : "payload"` (`occupancy.ts:726-747`). `commands.md:428` records the skip as deliberate. Claude Code, Cursor and Codex are all `payload` hosts — that is most of the "several multi-agent tabs" in the Origin.

**Failure mode.** Under rule 1 a payload-host child takes its own worktree, claims it, stamps `payload`, and is skipped on terminal. Nothing releases it; the parent's `occupancy:release` is per-path and never touches it. A build lands a documented close-out, AC3 goes green, and the lease pile grows one entry per spawn. (This is not `#3860`'s worktree pile — that non-goal does not cover leases.)

**Disposition consequence.** The skip's stated reason — "auto-release would drop a live parent lease mid-flight" — is a *same-tree* hazard, and rule 1 is exactly what removes it: release already compare-and-releases against `record.worktreePath` and `record.occupancyOwner` (`child-occupancy.ts:233-248`), so once the recorded tree is the child's own, a tree-scoped release is safe on the payload arm too. The issue should say so and name the `#3999` amendment as in scope, or state that AC3/AC4 are `host-env`-only. As written they read universal.

### F4 — The chokepoint proposed fix 1 asks for already exists and is deliberately held open

`sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** Spawn tools are a first-class PreToolUse family (`packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts:22-28`, `isSpawnTool`), and the dispatcher already denies them on posture (`spawn-not-ready`, `dispatcher.ts:1602`; read-only spawn deny, `dispatcher.ts:2313-2326`). Occupancy is the one verdict hardcoded open for them:

```ts
const occupancyGate = isSpawnTool(toolName)
  ? { allow: true, message: null, occupant: null, admitted: null }
  : evaluateOccupancyWriteGate(effectiveRoot, { ... });   // dispatcher.ts:1245-1257
```

`commands.md:429` states the same as posture ("spawn tools remain outside occupancy enforcement"), not as an absent surface.

**Failure mode.** As drafted, "fail closed if the child would share the primary checkout with a live foreign occupant" has no observer. It lands as AC1 skill/preamble text, and the only thing that actually fails closed stays the first-write denial — the denial the issue itself reports agents routing around into steal/re-prefix.

**Disposition consequence.** Restate proposed fix 1 against that seam: a spawn-time occupancy consult on `effectiveRoot`, deny when a live foreign occupant holds it and the spawn is implement-class. That is one branch on an existing gate with an existing deny vocabulary, and it is testable, which the preamble MUST is not. Keeping it as text is a legitimate choice — but then say so, and drop "fail closed".

### F5 — AC6's regression is green today against a string that has no recovery text

**Evidence (measured).** The cross-prefix refusal, in full:

```

owner's own host session (11111111-...-555555555555) under provider grok. That is a
```
